$schema_note: UK staircase plan-size reference. Source: Approved Doc K (England, 2013 revision). Verify against current published Doc K on gov.uk before use in real designs. Wales/Scotland/NI have their own regional documents.

doc_k_source.current_version: Approved Document K (2013 edition incorporating 2015 amendments)
doc_k_source.publisher: Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (gov.uk)
doc_k_source.verification_note: Numbers verified via canonical clause references (Philip 2026-07-25) + external HTML confirmation (tradecalculator.co.uk). PDF text not machine-readable from this environment; verbatim clause wording still to capture.

headroom_loft_exception.value: 1900mm central axis, 2000mm at one side, loft conversions only

doc_k_key_numbers_utility_stair._note: Utility stairs used in institutional/commercial settings — tighter than private-stair limits.

doc_k_key_numbers_common_stair._note: Common stairs serve multiple dwellings (communal flat-block hallway stair). Same limits as utility; typically also handrails both sides regardless of width.

professional_measurement_rules.rule_1_finished_floor_to_finished_floor: Rise is FINISHED-floor to FINISHED-floor. If floors not laid, maker must ask homeowner in writing what will be laid at both levels.
professional_measurement_rules.rule_2_nosing_not_part_of_going: Nosing overhang (typical 22-25 mm bullnose) is NOT part of the going. Going is measured riser-front to riser-front.
professional_measurement_rules.rule_3_rises_equals_goings_plus_one: Default: rises = goings + 1 (last rise takes you from top step onto landing). Exception: if top tread is designed level with landing, rises = goings.
professional_measurement_rules.rule_4_architrave_reduction: Reduce run by 20-25 mm per architrave at doorways top/bottom of flight.
professional_measurement_rules.rule_5_skirting_stringer_cut: String bottom edge is rebated for skirting board to continue past. Skirting height must be known at measure-up.
professional_measurement_rules.fitting_tolerance_notes: L-shape has more forgiveness because trimmer out-of-square is absorbed at the landing turn.

layouts.name: Quarter-turn with landing (L-shape)
layouts.description: Two flights at 90 degrees, joined by a small landing.

layouts.name: Quarter-turn with winders (L-shape space-saver)
layouts.description: Same 90-degree change but with wedge-shaped winder steps rather than a landing.
layouts.trade_off: Turn feels tighter; walking-line going must be checked carefully.

layouts.name: Half-turn with half-landing (U-shape / dogleg)
layouts.description: Two parallel flights heading opposite directions, joined by a half-landing (~2x flight width).

layouts.name: Half-turn with winders (compact dogleg)
layouts.description: 180-degree change with winder steps rather than a half-landing.

layouts.name: Split staircase (double-return)
layouts.description: One wide central flight to a large half-landing, then splits into two flights heading opposite directions to the upper floor.
layouts.reason_not_flippable: Symmetrical by design; flipping doesn't change the visible layout.

layouts.name: Spiral staircase
layouts.description: Circular flight around a central column.
layouts.doc_k_restriction: Permitted as sole staircase to habitable floor only under specific conditions. Best specified as secondary access.

layouts.name: Curved (helical) staircase
layouts.description: Sweeping continuous curve without a central column.
layouts.note: Walking-line going stays generous even on tight designs — the point of a helical vs a spiral. Top of the bespoke joinery market.

layouts.name: Floating cantilever staircase
layouts.description: Treads project directly from a load-bearing wall or hidden steel spine.
layouts.footprint_note: Same as the equivalent straight/half-turn layout — 'floating' refers to the visible structure, not the footprint.
layouts.structural_note: Requires engineered steel structure and load-tested plate brackets. Never a DIY specification.

paired_neighbour_mirror_rule.description: UK terraced houses typically mirror their internal layouts pair-by-pair to reduce inter-house sound transfer.
paired_neighbour_mirror_rule.right_side_of_pair: Staircase usually on LEFT of ground-floor plan; handrail typically against party wall.
paired_neighbour_mirror_rule.left_side_of_pair: Staircase usually on RIGHT; handrail typically against party wall.
paired_neighbour_mirror_rule.reliability: Almost always true for Victorian and Edwardian terraces. Less consistent on 20th-century estate builds.
